newsitem.title: UK: FKI says to buy BTR motor for 182.5 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: FKI says to buy BTR motor for 182.5 mln stg.

text.p: UK diversified engineering company FKI Plc said on Thursday it planned to buy motor firm Hawker Siddeley Electric Power Group from industrial conglomerate BTR for 182.5 million stg.

FKI, which said that it had wanted a significant UK acquisition to strengthen and complement its engineering group and boost UK earnings, noted the acquisition would be funded from existing resources.

The Hawker Siddeley Electric Power Group (HSEPG), whose brands include the Brush name, mainly consists of UK-based companies involved in the design, manufacture and sale of transformers, switchgear, generators, induction and synchronous motors for the power generation and distribution industries.

In a trading note, FKI said it had seen some recovery in the North American market since last year, and other markets remained "fairly solid". Results for the first four months of the year were in line with expectations and well ahead of the same period last year, it added.

HSEPG, whose operating profit before corporate charges has dived to 19.7 million stg on sales of 252.86 million last year from a profit of 31 million stg in 1993, also manufactures and sells railway locomotive and propulsion systems.

The price FKI is paying for HSEPG -- whose overseas operations span South Africa, Zimbabwe, Australia and France -- is based on the company's assumed net assets, which stood at 87.3 million stg last December.
FKI said HSEPG's profits had tumbled because it had decided against pursuing major new rail projects, which tend to have "unduly onerus commercial terms and technical specifications".

Last month, FKI announced it had conditionally agreed to buy leading Italian low voltage electric motors and alternators group Marelli for 34.6 million stg in a deal that included taking on 17.5 million stg of company debt.
That deal should be completed next month, it added.
FKI is holding an extraordinary meeting on October 3.
FKI said it planned to revamp the new unit along with its own engineering operations in the next two years to boost earnings and sales and cut costs.

"The directors believe that the complementary nature of many of the HSEPG's operations to those within the FKI Engineering Group will generate opportunities to restructure the combined operations over the next two years, reducing costs and increasing sales, purchasing and marketing efficiencies," FKI said in a statement.
"The directors believe that successful implementation of the programme will lead to earnings enhancements," it added.
